taxonomic_note: Older field guides and nursery sources may still use the former genus Gaura; preserve those names as synonyms but use current Oenothera placement canonically.
look_here_first: Look for the mismatch between plant size and flower size: a tall, densely velveteen annual carries a long crowded wand of extremely tiny flowers—only about 3 mm across.
project_tracker_diagnostic: annual or biennial, taprooted, not rosetted at flowering; 30–90+ cm tall; foliage and stems densely soft/velveteen hairy with glandular hairs; long terminal many-flowered spike/raceme; flowers only about 3 mm across; 4 tiny white petals aging light rose; narrow hard indehiscent fruit around 8 mm long

project_inclusion.range_basis: Hays — project Hays-local source pool contains 7 wild/noncultivated observations and flags the species as Hays Local; this is supporting occurrence evidence rather than a herbarium voucher. Travis — UT Plant Resources Center Travis County herbarium index includes Gaura parviflora, the homotypic synonym of Oenothera curtiflora. Williamson — UT Plant Resources Center Vascular Plants of Williamson County provides a detailed treatment under the accepted name Oenothera curtiflora.

comparisons.key_distinctions: Oenothera suffulta: Both are annual former-gauras. O. curtiflora is much more densely velveteen and its flowers are tiny (~3 mm); O. suffulta has 12–19 mm white flowers, a largely glabrous inflorescence, and a short chunky 4-lobed fruit. Oenothera lindheimeri: O. lindheimeri is a showy perennial with much larger flowers and an airy arching habit; O. curtiflora is a hairy annual with minute flowers.
